page: OVHcloud c2-60 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor based on the Haswell architecture without TSX, running at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, operating with a single thread per core to ensure predictable CPU allocation. The hardware configuration includes 60.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core, alongside a bundled 400 GB local SSD for storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks position the c2-60 in the average tier for multi-core and memory operations. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 8158.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 24191.73. Single-core performance is relatively weak, indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1093.0 and a text processing score of 1434.0. However, multi-threaded tasks such as bzip3 decompression at 142.69 GB/sec and software compilation with clang at 15531.0 perform within the average range. Large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 120.4 GB/sec, while write bandwidth is measured at 45.09 GB/sec.

Given the dedicated physical cores and balanced memory-to-core ratio, this instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, and database operations. It is less suited for single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM inference, where text generation speeds for a 7B model drop to 6.54 tokens/sec and large 70B model prompt processing is poor at 3.99 tokens/sec. The absence of hyperthreading ensures consistent CPU performance per core, offering a stable resource profile for compute-bound applications.
